image_description: A close-up view of a silver alloy car wheel with five spokes. Through the gaps in the spokes, a disk brake assembly is visible, including a perforated metal rotor and a dark caliper housing. The center cap features a logo (resembling Holden).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The circular shape of the rotor is clearly visible behind the wheel spokes. The perspective confirms it is a thin disc relative to its diameter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A dark, bulky mechanical component (the caliper) is visible clamping onto the outer edge of the rotor on the left side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wheel hub and lug bolts are completely occluded by the wheel's center cap and spokes; they cannot be seen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface shows cross-drilled holes, which is a common feature of high-performance ventilated rotors. While the internal fins aren't directly visible, the external features match the description of a performance rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Inside the caliper housing, the darker rectangular shape of the brake pad backing plate/friction material is discernible against the shiny rotor surface.
The hydraulic hose/line is typically located on the back or top of the caliper and is obscured by the wheel spoke and shadow in this angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct cross-drilled holes are clearly visible on the face of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor appears clean and silver/metallic. There is no obvious blueing or brown rust/discoloration indicative of heavy heat cycling or age.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has the rough, textured appearance typical of cast metal components found in automotive braking systems.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The logo on the center cap resembles a real-world brand (Holden lion and stone) but the details are slightly melted and indistinct, lacking the sharp vector precision of a real emblem. It is recognizable but structurally soft.
The reflections on the silver spokes are somewhat smeared and lack the crisp environmental mapping expected in a high-resolution photograph of polished metal.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific mechanical components (rotor, caliper) align with the 'disk brake' class label and distinguish from generic wheel parts.
To verify the spatial relationship between the wheel spokes and the brake rotor, ensuring the rotor sits correctly behind the spokes without geometric bleeding.
To check for boundary sharpness between the caliper and rotor, and ensure the drilled holes in the rotor are distinct, non-fused circles.
To assess overall photorealism, specifically looking for subtle AI artifacts in the metallic textures and lighting consistency.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of the cross-drilled holes on the rotor (check for melting/fusion).
Boundary separation between wheel spokes and the background brake components.
Logical consistency of the caliper mounting position relative to the rotor.
Quality of the center cap logo (potential text/symbol artifact).
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'cross-drilled' holes on the rotor. In AI images, these often deform into ovals or merge with the surface texture near the edges. Verify if the holes maintain consistent circular geometry despite the perspective angle. Also, scrutinize the center logo for 'almost-right' but failed symbol generation.
